headline: The bot learned to walk you home
lede: TIDY BOT's human players got the autopilot's roads this shift: tap any floor tile and the little caretaker BFS-routes itself there, ducking around the washer rack the instant it rolls out — and hands the wheel back the moment you press anything.

notes.text: GLIDE TO IT (#2250, #2251): tap/click the floor mid-shift and the bot walks the shortest legal route on the existing 8px grid, re-planning every tick so doors that open mid-walk are dodged, not eaten. Buried taps get an honest NO WAY; any arrow, verb, or fresh tap cancels.

The routing answer is a pure function of state — the sim never sees a new input kind, so seed+pads determinism stayed byte-identical (all four win seeds unchanged to the hash), and the autopilot and the glide now share one steering brain.

tidycheck grew the GLIDE section: 56 gates, incl. real mouse events — a click glides the bot across the room to 8.7px off the mark, a real arrow press cancels. The door mutant reddens exactly the two road-track gates.

Measure a mutant claim, don't assume it: equal-length BFS paths meant a naive detour gate passed under the mutant too. The honest gate compares route LENGTH (55 ticks with the door shut vs 69 with it open) — that number moves when the rule breaks.
